questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Austria?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Austria article.

questions.proof: The capital of Austria is Vienna (Wien).

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Austria?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Austria on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Austria article.

questions.proof: Around Austria are the countries of Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Austria?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Austria article.

questions.proof: The people in Austria speak German, a few also speak Hungarian, Slovenian and Croatian.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Austria?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Austria article.

questions.proof: Austria, officially the Republic of Austria, is a country in Central Europe.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In the Neolithic Age people, lived there to dig for mineral resources, especially copper. Ötzi, a mummy found in a glacier between Austria and _____, is from that time.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Austria”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Ancient times” part of the Austria article.

questions.proof: In the Neolithic Age people, lived there to dig for mineral resources, especially copper. Ötzi, a mummy found in a glacier between Austria and Italy, is from that time.
